channel.title: Blockfront
channel.description: Blockfront reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, DeFi protocols, exchanges, regulation, security incidents, funding rounds and network upgrades.

item.title: Why Crypto Treasury Transfers Take Multi-Hop Routes
item.description: Treasury transfers take multi-hop routes when direct paths lack liquidity, supported tokens or affordable settlement; each added hop brings another fee, delay and point of failure.

item.title: How to choose a safer cross-chain settlement method
item.description: For safer cross-chain settlement, compare who verifies the transfer, what asset arrives, and how long withdrawals take before choosing speed or fees on the destination chain.

item.title: Cross-network address confusion comes down to the chain
item.description: The same wallet address can appear on several blockchains, but each chain keeps separate balances, tokens and transactions. Check the network before sending funds.

item.title: QuickSwap swaps: when to execute now or wait
item.description: Choose a market route for a swap that should execute now; use a limit or DCA order when price or timing matters more than immediate execution on QuickSwap.

item.title: A Token Migration Can Change the Asset a Swap Delivers
item.description: A token migration can leave a cross-chain swap pointing at an old contract. Check the route, migration terms and settlement status before sending funds.

item.title: How to Verify a Cross-Chain Swap Has Finished
item.description: Check the source transaction, destination-chain receipt and wallet balance; a bridge status page alone may not prove the swap has completed successfully.

item.title: Where Your Coins Go in a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: A cross-chain swap sends your input to a source-chain vault, routes value through liquidity pools and pays out the target asset from a destination-chain vault.

item.title: What cross-chain treasury transfer limits control
item.description: Cross-chain treasury limits cap each transfer and total flow; understanding how they refill helps teams plan liquidity, timing and approval thresholds.

item.title: EBA names Circle’s USDC EU’s first significant e-money token
item.description: The EBA classified Circle’s USDC as the EU’s first significant e-money token, shifting oversight of reserves, liquidity and redemption plans from France on Nov. 12.

item.title: Fireblocks Launches Stablecoin Liquidity Market for Payments Firms
item.description: Fireblocks launched Liquidity Market on Oct. 15, letting firms compare stablecoin quotes across OTC desks and settle directly, with no spread charged by Fireblocks.

item.title: Why cross-chain swaps take longer than token swaps
item.description: A token swap settles on one blockchain; a cross-chain swap must also move value between networks, wait for verification and execute on the destination chain.

item.title: How bridge-and-swap routing handles repeat transfers
item.description: Bridge-and-swap routing combines a cross-chain transfer with a token exchange; repeat payments save setup time, but each run still needs checks on route, fees and output.

item.title: Wallet address formats show where a transfer can go
item.description: Wallet formats reveal how chains encode accounts, but matching addresses do not guarantee matching networks; check the chain and asset before sending.

item.title: Ledger tightens wallet sales rules after $86 million theft estimate
item.description: Ledger is tightening reseller rules after tampered wallets exposed recovery phrases; an onchain estimate puts losses above $86 million, but the total is unverified.

item.title: Pool fees and bridge charges add up differently on frequent swaps
item.description: Pool fees apply to each swap, while bridge costs apply to moving assets between chains; compare the route’s total cost and net output before trading.

item.title: How to Check a Relay Bridge Quote Before Sending
item.description: Compare the destination amount, fees, route, expiry and token details in a bridge quote, then verify the wallet prompt before approving or sending.

item.title: Acrossbridge for wallet beginners: how to choose a route
item.description: Choose a cross-chain route by matching the source asset, destination network and final token, then compare the steps, costs and risks before you sign.

item.title: Biswap in 2026: How to choose a cross-chain route
item.description: A cross-chain route should be judged by the asset delivered, total cost, execution time and failure path, with biswap handling a move that also needs a swap.

item.title: Polymarket starts V2 canary with unified positions and pUSD
item.description: Polymarket has started production canary markets for V2, unifying positions in one ERC-1155 contract and using pUSD collateral before a planned November switch.

item.title: Binance rolls out free AI interface after 150,000-user beta
item.description: Binance has rolled out its free AI trading interface to English-language users after about 150,000 people tested it, with more language support still to come.
